summary: Hong Kong's original Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (Oct 2003 to its suspension on 15 Jan 2015; HK$6.5m, then HK$10m in financial assets only from Oct 2010) is well documented through Legislative Council replies, archived Immigration Department quarterly statistics (cumulative applications, approvals by applicant category, investment) and ImmD annual-report visa counts; the New CIES (from 1 Mar 2024; HK$30m incl. HK$3m in a government-run portfolio) has only occasional cumulative press-release and LegCo figures, with country breakdowns for 2024-2025 led by Guinea-Bissau and Vanuatu. Taiwan has investor-residence routes in law (NT$6m for Hong Kong/Macao residents; NT$15m business or NT$30m bonds for foreigners' permanent residence) but no official counts were found.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (with spouse and children under 18)
program_terms.quote: Persons with net assets under their control and disposal for investment of no less than HK$6.5 million in permissible investment assets will be eligible for admission into Hong Kong as capital investment entrants.
program_terms.notes: Any mix of Hong Kong real estate (residential, commercial, industrial, land) and specified financial assets (HK$ equities, debt securities, certificates of deposit, subordinated debt, eligible collective investment schemes). Applicants also had to hold net assets of at least HK$6.5m for the two years before applying (hkg-legco-se-paper-cies-2010, para 6). No top-up required if the portfolio falls in value.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (with spouse and children under 18)
program_terms.quote: The threshold of investment (and net assets/net equity requirement) for admission to Hong Kong under the CIES is raised from HK$6.5 million to HK$10 million; and ii) Real estate is suspended temporarily as a class of Permissible Investment Assets (PIA) under the CIES.
program_terms.notes: Real estate no longer counted for new applications; the net-assets requirement rose to HK$10m as well. Applications with at least HK$6.5m invested in the six months before 14 Oct 2010 were still accepted under the old rules (transitional arrangement). valid_to: the day before the 15 Jan 2015 suspension (hkg-isd-pr-cies-suspension-2015).

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (with spouse/partner and children under 18)
program_terms.quote: An applicant must make investment of a minimum of HK$30 million in the permissible investment assets
program_terms.notes: Made up of at least HK$27m in permissible assets plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio (see the two rows below). Applicants must also show net assets of at least HK$30m: throughout the two years before applying until 28 Feb 2025, throughout six months from 1 Mar 2025 (hkg-legco-lcq9-new-cies-2025). Launch date from hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-opens-2024.

program_terms.quote: An applicant must invest a minimum of HK$27 million in any of the following permissible assets
program_terms.notes: Listed HK$/RMB equities and debt, certificates of deposit (capped at 10% of the threshold), subordinated debt, SFC-authorised funds, REITs and investment-linked assurance, open-ended fund companies, limited partnership funds, and non-residential real estate capped at HK$10m. From 1 Mar 2025 assets may be held through a family-owned investment holding vehicle (hkg-fstb-pr-new-cies-enhancements-2025).

program_terms.quote: each applicant under the new CIES is required to place HK$3 million into a new CIES Investment Portfolio (“Portfolio”), which will be set up and managed by the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited.
program_terms.notes: Invested in companies/projects with a Hong Kong nexus (innovation and technology, strategic industries). Capital preservation and dividends are not guaranteed.

program_terms.quote: with effect from October 16, 2024, an applicant under the New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES) is allowed to invest in residential properties, provided that the transaction price of a single property must be HK$50 million or above.
program_terms.notes: Minimum is the price of the property, not the amount counted: all real estate together counts for at most HK$10m towards the HK$30m threshold.

program_terms.applies_to: Hong Kong or Macao resident applicant
program_terms.quote: 五、在臺灣地區有新臺幣六百萬元以上之投資，經中央目的事業主管機關審查通過

program_terms.notes: 'Exceeding' NT$15 million, plus at least five jobs for ROC nationals for three years. Gives permanent residence (Alien Permanent Resident Certificate) directly.

events.title: Capital Investment Entrant Scheme opens
events.description: The CIES starts receiving applications: residence for people investing at least HK$6.5 million in Hong Kong property or financial assets without running a business. Open to foreign nationals, Macao residents, Taiwan residents, stateless persons and Chinese nationals with permanent residence abroad, but not to Mainland residents because of foreign-exchange controls. Announced on 30 Sept 2003.
events.quote: The Government today (September 30) announced that the Capital Investment Entrant Scheme will start receiving applications on October 27, 2003.

events.title: Investment-linked insurance products allowed as eligible funds
events.description: Scheme rules refined so that investment-linked assurance scheme (ILAS) products issued by Class C insurers can count as eligible collective investment schemes.
events.location: section 'Refinement to the Rules ... relating to investment-linked assurance scheme products'
events.quote: The refined Scheme Rules are available at http://www.immd.gov.hk/ehtm/hkvisas_13_5.htm from 6 July 2010. They come into force on the same date.

events.title: Threshold raised to HK$10 million; property no longer counts
events.description: After a review, the minimum investment (and net-assets requirement) rises from HK$6.5m to HK$10m and real estate is suspended as a permissible asset. The government later told LegCo the property suspension was announced in the 13 Oct 2010 Policy Address 'in view of public concern on property prices and opinions of the Legislative Council members' (hkg-legco-lcq7-cies-2011).
events.quote: The Government announced today (October 13) that following a review, the following amendments will be introduced to the Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (CIES) with effect from October 14, 2010

events.title: Capital Investment Entrant Scheme suspended
events.description: The CIES is suspended 'until further notice'. Reasons given: it was introduced in 2003 during a recession to attract capital; attracting capital investors 'should no longer be our priority', the focus should be talent, professionals and entrepreneurs; and suspension would help ImmD clear over 12,000 pending applications. Pending and approved applications were unaffected; a transitional arrangement accepted applications for investments made in the six months before 15 Jan 2015.
events.quote: In view of the latest economic situation in Hong Kong, attracting capital investment entrants should no longer be our priority. Instead, our focus should be on attracting talent, professionals and innovative entrepreneurs to contribute to our economy.

events.title: All remaining CIES applications finalised

programs.name: Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (CIES; 資本投資者入境計劃)
programs.notes: Residence (not citizenship) for people who invest in Hong Kong without running a business there; run by the Immigration Department under the 'Rules for the Capital Investment Entrant Scheme' (ID(E)968); no law establishing it was found. Threshold HK$6.5m in property and/or financial assets from 27 Oct 2003; HK$10m in financial assets only from 14 Oct 2010. Open to foreign nationals, Macao and Taiwan residents, stateless persons and Chinese nationals holding permanent residence abroad (not Mainland residents). Two steps: approval-in-principle (enter as a visitor to invest within six months), then formal approval and two-year permissions to stay, renewed if the investment is kept. After seven years' continuous ordinary residence investors and dependants could apply for the right of abode (permanent residence) under the Basic Law. Suspended 'until further notice' from 15 Jan 2015; applications already received were still processed and all were finalised in October 2023. The large majority of applicants were Chinese nationals with foreign permanent residence; of those formally approved to end-2007, the largest groups held permanent residence in Gambia (414 of 1,114), Canada, New Zealand, Nauru, Australia, the Philippines, Niger and Guinea-Bissau (LCQ12, 2008).

programs.name: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES; 新資本投資者入境計劃)
programs.notes: Residence for investors of at least HK$30m: HK$27m in permissible financial assets and/or real estate (real estate counts for at most HK$10m; residential only for single properties of HK$50m+ from 16 Oct 2024) plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio managed by the Hong Kong Investment Corporation. Approved by the Executive Council on 19 Dec 2023; no law establishing it was found. InvestHK verifies net assets (HK$30m, held two years before applying until Feb 2025, six months from 1 Mar 2025) and the investment; ImmD grants approval-in-principle (180-day visitor stay to invest), then formal approval: 2 years' stay, then 3-year extensions. After seven years' continuous ordinary residence applicants and dependants may apply for permanent residence; those who keep the investment seven years without meeting the residence test may apply for unconditional stay. Eligible: foreign nationals (except Afghanistan, Cuba, North Korea), Chinese nationals with foreign permanent residence, Macao residents, Chinese residents of Taiwan. Official figures are cumulative press-release totals; the only country breakdowns found (May 2024, March 2025) are led by Guinea-Bissau and Vanuatu.

programs.name: Taiwan residence for Hong Kong and Macao residents through investment (香港澳門居民進入臺灣地區及居留定居許可辦法 第16條第1項第5款)
programs.notes: Under Article 16(1)(5) of the Ministry of the Interior's regulations for Hong Kong and Macao residents (first issued 30 June 1997), a Hong Kong or Macao resident who invests NT$6 million or more in Taiwan, approved by the central competent authority, may apply for residence. Under Article 29 a resident may apply for settlement (registered permanent residence, i.e. a Taiwan household registration and ROC citizenship rights) after one year of continuous residence, or two years with at least 270 days a year, while still meeting the original conditions. Applicants who were formerly Mainland residents or who worked for Mainland party, state or military bodies may be refused (Article 22). The start date of the NT$6m investment ground, and any official count of residence or settlement permits granted on it, were not found. The Mainland Affairs Council publishes only totals of Hong Kong residents granted residence and settlement for all reasons.

programs.name: Taiwan permanent residence for foreign investment immigrants (入出國及移民法 第25條第4項; Alien Permanent Resident Certificate / Plum Blossom Card)
programs.notes: Article 25(4) of the Immigration Act lets foreigners apply to the National Immigration Agency for 'investment immigration'; once approved and the investment is made, permanent residence is granted directly, without the usual five years' prior residence. NIA guidelines set the thresholds: more than NT$15 million in a profitable business creating jobs for at least five ROC nationals for three years, or more than NT$30 million in central government bonds held three years. Spouses and children under 18 may apply with the investor. Permanent residence is not citizenship; naturalisation is a separate process. No official count of investment-immigration grants was found, and the date this route began was not established.

new_indicators.definition: Applications that hold an approval-in-principle (permission to enter and make the qualifying investment) but have not yet received final/formal approval, counted at a date. A stock, not a running total of approvals-in-principle ever granted.

gaps: Original CIES: no official year-by-year series of applications received after 2009, nor of formal approvals by year for 2010-2014; only cumulative quarterly snapshots (Dec 2012 to Jun 2014, archived ImmD pages) and visas issued per year (ImmD annual reports 2010 onwards). The ImmD statistics page for Sept and Dec 2014 and any final end-of-scheme totals (total applications, total approvals, total investment 2003-2015) were not found in archived copies.
Original CIES: ImmD annual-report visa figures for 2003-2009 were not collected (older annual reports are in a different format; see leads).

Original CIES: no official lifetime investment total found; the only figure (HK$314.5 billion) is from an industry article and is recorded as a claim. Last official figure: HK$192.7 billion in formal-approval cases at 30 June 2014.
Original CIES: nationality of approved Chinese-national applicants by country of permanent residence is available only to end-2007 (LCQ12, 2008); no later country breakdowns found.
Original CIES: no official data on revocations, persons removed for breaching investment rules, or dependants granted the right of abode (ImmD says it does not keep dependants' figures).

New CIES: no regular statistics release; figures come from occasional InvestHK press releases, LegCo replies and ImmD annual reviews, with different stage definitions and cut-off dates. Country breakdowns exist only for applications to end-May 2024 and for ImmD entry applications made in March 2025; no nationality breakdown of formal approvals.

New CIES: the 'expected investment amount' figures are projections (applications times HK$30m), not money invested; verified investment is published only occasionally (end-Feb 2025, end-Apr 2025, end-Feb 2026).
New CIES: number of applications rejected or withdrawn overall is not published (only 'none rejected' for the March 2025 cohort).

Taiwan: two investor-residence routes exist in law (Hong Kong/Macao residents investing NT$6m; foreigners' permanent residence for NT$15m business investment with five jobs, or NT$30m government bonds), but no official count of permits granted on investment grounds was found. Mainland Affairs Council open data gives only all-reason totals of Hong Kong residents granted residence and settlement. A Control Yuan (監察院) investigation report on Hong Kong/Macao 'investment immigration' was found in search results but its download link returned an error (download blocked/not available).
Taiwan: the dates on which the NT$6m (Hong Kong/Macao) and NT$15m/NT$30m (foreigners) thresholds were introduced were not established.
